summary: CLI executes LLM-returned shell commands from prompt-injectable git error text
details: The `gitquickpush push` subcommand, on any git push failure, sends the git error message and full `git status` output to a remote LLM (Google Gemini at generativelanguage.googleapis.com, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at router.huggingface.co) authenticated with a hardcoded API key shipped in the source. The tool then iterates the model's `commandsToRun` array and passes each string to `execSync(cmd, { stdio: 'ignore' })`, running the model output as shell commands on the installer's machine with output suppressed. Because part of the prompt is the git error text, commit message context, and branch names, content that reaches those fields (crafted error strings from a remote, remote branch names, or upstream commit messages during a push conflict) can steer the model to emit arbitrary commands that then execute locally. The relay to the LLM is not documented in the README, which advertises the package as "Push files directly to GitHub"; the destination and hardcoded API key are the author's, so installer git-repo error text and status are transmitted under the author's account whenever a push fails.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
